## Scope

By the end of this session, you will be able to:

::: {.incremental}
- **Wrangle** messy clinical data using `dplyr` and `tidyr`
- **Summarize** patient data into publication-ready tables with `gtsummary`
- **Visualize** results with `ggplot2`
- **Apply** these skills hands-on using real medical datasets
:::

::: aside
*Taming the Data Beast*, by Allison Horst
:::

## Overview

| Section | What You'll Learn |
|---|---|
| 🧹 **Data Cleaning** | Separating columns, fixing types, adding flags |
| 📊 **Summary Tables** | `tbl_summary()` with p-values and group comparisons |
| 💻 **Your Turn** | 3 exercises using the `blood_storage` cancer dataset |

## Why R? {.center}

::: {.incremental}
- You've probably already done this in Excel 👇
  - Sort by a column, delete some rows, calculate a mean, make a chart
- R does **all of that** — in about 3 lines of code
- And unlike Excel, your work is **reproducible, shareable, and reviewable**
:::

## The Lego Brick: One Line of R

```{r}
#| label: cleaning-demo-0
#| echo: true
#| output-location: column
#| code-line-numbers: "1"

library(medicaldata)

blood_storage
```

::: {.fragment}
That's it. That prints your dataset. R is just **instructions in plain English-ish**.
:::

::: {.incremental}
- `filter(Age > 60)` → keep rows where Age is over 60
- `mutate(high_psa = PreopPSA >= 10)` → add a new column
- `select(Age, Grade)` → keep only those two columns
:::

## The Pipe `|>` {.center}

The pipe reads as **"and then"**. It chains steps together:

```r
blood_storage |>         # start with the data, and then...
  filter(Age > 60) |>   # keep older patients, and then...
  select(Age, Grade)    # show just these two columns
```

## You Already Know More Than You Think

Most of the R you'll use today maps directly to questions you already ask:

| English question | R code |
|---|---|
| "Show me only Grade 4 patients" | `filter(Grade == 4)` |
| "Add a column for high PSA" | `mutate(high_psa = PreopPSA >= 10)` |
| "What's the average age?" | `summarize(mean_age = mean(Age))` |
| "Make a table by treatment group" | `tbl_summary(by = trt)` |

::: {.fragment}
Today's goal isn't memorization — it's **pattern recognition**.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
All code runs **live in your browser** — no R installation needed today!
:::

## The "Real-World" Medical Researcher Problem

You are a resident on a busy clinical rotation. You've been handed a
messy Vital Signs log from a 3-patient pilot study.

- **The Data:** A CSV with blood pressure stored as `"128/78"` and temperatures like `"98.6F"`
- **The Goal:**
  - Split blood pressure into systolic and diastolic columns
  - Remove the `"F"` from Temperature
  - Flag any patient with systolic BP ≥ 140
  - Make a bar chart of all Systolic BPs
- ⏱️ **You have 2 minutes**

## 

```{r}
#| label: reveal-cleaning
#| echo: false
library(tidyverse)

# Secretly create the messy data for the demo
messy_vitals <- tibble::tibble(
  patient = c("Gemma Dunn", "Priscilla Holding", "Aniya Warner"),
  bp = c("128/78", "148/92", "115/73"),
  temp = c("98.6F", "101.2F", "97.5F")
)
```

## {auto-animate="true"}

```{r}
#| label: cleaning-demo-1
#| echo: true
#| output-location: column
#| code-line-numbers: "1"

print(messy_vitals)
```

## {auto-animate="true"}

```{r}
#| label: cleaning-demo-2
#| echo: true
#| output-location: column
#| code-line-numbers: "2-3"

messy_vitals |>
  # Separate BP into systolic and diastolic
  separate(bp, into = c("sys", "dia"), sep = "/")
```

## {auto-animate="true"}

```{r}
#| label: cleaning-demo-3
#| echo: true
#| output-location: column
#| code-line-numbers: "4-5"

messy_vitals |>
  # Separate BP into systolic and diastolic
  separate(bp, into = c("sys", "dia"), sep = "/") |>
  # Strip the "F" unit from temperature
  mutate(temp = parse_number(temp))
```

## {auto-animate="true"}

```{r}
#| label: cleaning-demo-4
#| echo: true
#| output-location: column
#| code-line-numbers: "6-7"

messy_vitals |>
  # Separate BP into systolic and diastolic
  separate(bp, into = c("sys", "dia"), sep = "/") |>
  # Strip the "F" unit from temperature
  mutate(temp = parse_number(temp)) |>
  # Convert BP columns from character to numeric
  mutate(across(c(sys, dia), as.numeric))
```

## {auto-animate="true"}

```{r}
#| label: cleaning-demo-5
#| echo: true
#| output-location: column
#| code-line-numbers: "8-9"

messy_vitals |>
  # Separate BP into systolic and diastolic
  separate(bp, into = c("sys", "dia"), sep = "/") |>
  # Strip the "F" unit from temperature
  mutate(temp = parse_number(temp)) |>
  # Convert BP columns from character to numeric
  mutate(across(c(sys, dia), as.numeric)) |>
  # Flag patients with elevated systolic BP (≥ 140)
  mutate(flag = sys >= 140)
```

## {auto-animate="true"}

```{r}
#| label: cleaning-demo-6
#| echo: true
#| output-location: column
#| code-line-numbers: "10-12"

messy_vitals |>
  # Separate BP into systolic and diastolic
  separate(bp, into = c("sys", "dia"), sep = "/") |>
  # Strip the "F" unit from temperature
  mutate(temp = parse_number(temp)) |>
  # Convert BP columns from character to numeric
  mutate(across(c(sys, dia), as.numeric)) |>
  # Flag patients with elevated systolic BP (≥ 140)
  mutate(flag = sys >= 140) |>
  # Visualize
  ggplot(aes(x = patient, y = sys, fill = flag)) +
  geom_col()
```

## {auto-animate="true"}

```{r}
#| label: cleaning-demo-7
#| echo: true
#| output-location: column
#| code-line-numbers: "13-14"

messy_vitals |>
  # Separate BP into systolic and diastolic
  separate(bp, into = c("sys", "dia"), sep = "/") |>
  # Strip the "F" unit from temperature
  mutate(temp = parse_number(temp)) |>
  # Convert BP columns from character to numeric
  mutate(across(c(sys, dia), as.numeric)) |>
  # Flag patients with elevated systolic BP (≥ 140)
  mutate(flag = sys >= 140) |>
  # Visualize
  ggplot(aes(x = patient, y = sys, fill = flag)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("gray", "#990000")) + # IU Crimson!
  theme_minimal()
```

## Another Challenge

You are a resident on a busy clinical rotation. You've been handed a
messy cancer treatment outcomes dataset.

- **The Data:** The `trial` dataset — 200 patients, 2 treatment arms
- **The Goal:**
  - Summarize patient characteristics (age, tumor grade, treatment response)
  - Split summaries by treatment group
  - Report mean ± SD for continuous variables
  - Calculate p-values for group comparisons
- ⏱️ **You have 2 minutes**

## {auto-animate="true"} 

```{r}
#| label: table-demo-1
#| echo: true
#| output-location: column
#| code-line-numbers: "4-7"

library(gtsummary)

# Use the built-in 'trial' clinical dataset
gtsummary::trial |>
  select(trt, age, grade, response) |>
  # Create the summary table
  tbl_summary()
```

## {auto-animate="true"} 

```{r}
#| label: table-demo-2
#| echo: true
#| output-location: column
#| code-line-numbers: "8-9"

library(gtsummary)

# Use the built-in 'trial' clinical dataset
gtsummary::trial |>
  select(trt, age, grade, response) |>
  # Create the summary table
  tbl_summary(
    # Split by treatment group
    by = trt,
  )
```

## {auto-animate="true"} 

```{r}
#| label: table-demo-3
#| echo: true
#| output-location: column
#| code-line-numbers: "10-11"

library(gtsummary)

# Use the built-in 'trial' clinical dataset
gtsummary::trial |>
  select(trt, age, grade, response) |>
  # Create the summary table
  tbl_summary(
    # Split by treatment group
    by = trt,
    # Report mean ± SD for continuous variables
    statistic = list(all_continuous() ~ "{mean} ({sd})")
  )
```

## {auto-animate="true"} 

```{r}
#| label: table-demo-4
#| echo: true
#| output-location: column
#| code-line-numbers: "13-14"

library(gtsummary)

# Use the built-in 'trial' clinical dataset
gtsummary::trial |>
  select(trt, age, grade, response) |>
  # Create the summary table
  tbl_summary(
    # Split by treatment group
    by = trt,
    # Report mean ± SD for continuous variables
    statistic = list(all_continuous() ~ "{mean} ({sd})")
  ) |>
  # Add statistical comparison (p-values)
  add_p()
```

## {auto-animate="true"} 

```{r}
#| label: table-demo-5

#| output-location: column

library(gtsummary)

# Use the built-in 'trial' clinical dataset
gtsummary::trial |>
  select(trt, age, grade, response) |>
  # Create the summary table
  tbl_summary(
    # Split by treatment group
    by = trt,
    # Report mean ± SD for continuous variables
    statistic = list(all_continuous() ~ "{mean} ({sd})")
  ) |>
  # Add statistical comparison (p-values)
  add_p() |>
  # Add a "Total" column
  add_overall()
```

## {auto-animate="true"} 

```{r}
#| label: table-demo-6
#| echo: true
#| output-location: column

library(gtsummary)

# Use the built-in 'trial' clinical dataset
gtsummary::trial |>
  select(trt, age, grade, response) |>
  # Create the summary table
  tbl_summary(
    # Split by treatment group
    by = trt,
    label = list(
      age ~ "Patient Age",
      grade ~ "Tumor Grade",
      response ~ "Treatment Response"
    ),
    # Report mean ± SD for continuous variables
    statistic = list(all_continuous() ~ "{mean} ({sd})")
  ) |>
  # Add statistical comparison (p-values)
  add_p() |>
  # Add a "Total" column
  add_overall() |>
  # Make it look professional
  bold_labels() |>
  modify_header(label = "**Variable**")
```

## Exercise 1: Isolate High-Grade Tumors {.scrollable}

The `blood_storage` dataset contains a `Grade` variable (1–4). Filter the data to show only the most aggressive tumors (**Grade 4**) and assign it to `high_grade_cancers`.

:::{.fragment}
```{webr}
#| exercise: medex_1
# Filter for Grade 4 tumors
high_grade_cancers <- blood_storage |> 
  filter(Grade == ____)

# Count the results
nrow(high_grade_cancers)
```

::: { .solution exercise="medex_1"} 
::: { .callout-tip collapse=false}

```{webr}
#| exercise: medex_1
#| solution: true
high_grade_cancers <- blood_storage |> 
  filter(Grade == 4)

nrow(high_grade_cancers)
```

:::
:::

```{webr}
#| exercise: medex_1
#| check: true
gradethis::grade_this_code()
```

:::

## Exercise 2: Defining Clinical Risk {.scrollable}

A PSA (Prostate Specific Antigen) level $\ge$ 10 is often considered high risk. Use `mutate()` to create a new column called `high_psa` that is `TRUE` if `PreopPSA` is 10 or greater.

:::{.fragment}

```{webr}
#| exercise: medex_2
# Create a logical flag for high PSA
psa_analysis <- blood_storage |> 
  mutate(high_psa = ___ >= 10)

# View the first few rows
head(psa_analysis)
```

::: { .solution exercise="med_ex_2"} 
::: { .callout-tip collapse=false}

```{webr}
#| exercise: medex_2
#| solution: true
psa_analysis <- blood_storage |> 
  mutate(high_psa = PreopPSA >= 10)

head(psa_analysis)
```

:::
:::

```{webr}
#| exercise: medex_2
#| check: true
gradethis::grade_this_code()
```

## Exercise 3: Complex Data Preparation {.scrollable}

The PI wants to look at younger patients (Age $\le$ 60) who had a cancer recurrence (`Recurrence == 1`). Select only those patients and calculate their average PSA.

:::{.fragment}
```{webr}
#| exercise: medex_3
# Combine filter and summarize
summary_stats <- blood_storage |> 
  filter(Age <= 60, ___ == 1) |> 
  summarize(mean_psa = ___(PreopPSA, na.rm = TRUE))

summary_stats
```

::: { .solution exercise="medex_3"} 
::: { .callout-tip collapse=false}

```{webr}
#| exercise: medex_3
#| solution: true
summary_stats <- blood_storage |> 
  filter(Age <= 60, Recurrence == 1) |> 
  summarize(mean_psa = mean(PreopPSA, na.rm = TRUE))

summary_stats
```

::: 
:::

```{webr}
#| exercise: medex_3
#| check: true
gradethis::grade_this_code()
```

:::

## Recap & Key Takeaways

::: {.incremental}
- 🧹 **`tidyr::separate()`** splits combined columns (e.g., blood pressure)
- 🔢 **`dplyr::mutate()`** creates and transforms columns
- 📊 **`gtsummary::tbl_summary()`** produces publication-ready clinical tables in seconds
- 📈 **`ggplot2`** turns tidy data into polished visuals with a few lines of code
- 💡 The **pipe `|>`** chains steps cleanly — read it as *"and then..."*
:::

::: {.fragment}
**Next steps:** Try these on your own research data. The skills transfer directly.
:::
